model_annotation: The image displays a donut chart with two concentric rings, representing two different metrics related to ambiguity. The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity Std (Outer)", is divided into four segments, each corresponding to a standard deviation value: Std: 0.0 (darkest blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (medium-dark blue, 39.0%), Std: 0.82 (medium blue, 7.0%), and Std: 0.94 (lightest blue, 5.0%). The inner ring, labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)", is divided into three segments: Max: 1 (light blue, 47.7%), Max: 2 (lighter blue, 38.0%), and Max: 3 (very light blue, 14.2%). Each segment in both rings is labeled with its percentage value, and the chart includes two legends on the right side to explain the color coding for each metric. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, and the percentages sum to 100% for each ring. The chart uses varying shades of blue to distinguish between categories, with darker shades representing lower standard deviation values and lighter shades representing higher maximum ambiguity values.
